subject: Language Usage

units.title: Argument: Claims, Opposing Claims, Evidence and Cohesion
skills: Introduce a claim and distinguish it from alternate or opposing claims
Support claims with logical reasoning and relevant evidence from credible sources
Use words, phrases and clauses to create cohesion and show relationships
Organize problem-and-solution and cause-and-effect explanations
vocab: claim
the arguable position the writer will defend
opposing claim
a position that disagrees with the writer and must be recognized and answered
rebuttal
the part of an argument that explains why the opposing claim is weaker
cohesion
the way sentences and ideas connect so that a text reads as one whole
relevant evidence
evidence that directly supports the specific point being made
problem-and-solution structure
a way of organizing that describes a problem, its causes and possible solutions

passage.title: AI Tools and Homework
passage.intro: Rakan is writing an argument essay for his English class. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Artificial intelligence tools can now write essays, solve math problems and summarize books in seconds. (2) Some educators want to ban these tools completely, while others believe students should use them freely. (3) I believe schools should allow AI tools for homework, but only with clear rules. (4) When students use AI to explain difficult ideas, they can learn at their own pace. (5) Copying an AI answer without understanding it teaches nothing. (6) Teachers could require students to describe how they used AI and what they learned. (7) Smartphones were first introduced in the early 2000s. (8) With thoughtful rules, AI can become a tutor rather than a shortcut.

items.stem: Which sentence states Rakan’s claim?
options: sentence 1
sentence 2
sentence 3
sentence 4
items.skill: States a clear claim or thesis

items.stem: Which sentence should be removed because it is not relevant to the argument?
options: sentence 4
sentence 5
sentence 6
sentence 7
items.skill: Identifies a sentence that does not belong

items.stem: How does sentence 2 help the argument?
options: It shows that there are different opinions before the writer states his own.
It gives evidence that AI tools always produce correct answers for students.
It explains how AI tools are built and trained by computer engineers.
It states the conclusion that the whole essay will try to prove.
items.skill: States a clear claim or thesis

items.stem: Which transition would BEST begin sentence 5 to create cohesion?
options: In the very same way,

items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which piece of evidence would BEST support sentence 4?
options: Artificial intelligence has appeared in many science fiction movies and novels over the past fifty years.
Many technology companies are competing to create the most popular AI tools for people of all ages around the world.
Some students prefer to do their homework in the evening, while others prefer to do it early in the morning.
In one study, students who used an AI tutor to review algebra scored higher on a later test than those who did not.
items.skill: Chooses relevant evidence to support a point

items.stem: Which source would be the MOST credible for evidence about AI and learning?
options: a comment on a forum by someone who does not give a name
a research article from a university’s education department
a blog written by a company that sells an AI homework app
a video of a student who says AI is the best invention ever

passage.title: Urban Heat Islands
passage.intro: Joury is writing an informative report about a problem and its solutions. Read her draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) On a summer afternoon, a city center can be several degrees hotter than the countryside around it. (2) Scientists call this effect an urban heat island. (3) Dark roads and rooftops absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night. (4) In addition, cities have fewer trees to provide shade and cool the air. (5) Higher temperatures increase the use of air conditioners, which raises energy costs and pollution. (6) Fortunately, there are several solutions. (7) Some cities are painting rooftops white, planting trees along streets and building parks to bring temperatures down.

items.stem: How is Joury’s report mainly organized?
options: by comparing two cities in different parts of the world
by describing a problem, its causes and possible solutions
by telling the story of a scientist in the order of events
by listing the steps for building a new city park

sentence 4
sentence 6

options: Instead
However
Therefore
Furthermore
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: What is the purpose of sentence 6?
options: to restate the definition given in sentence 2
to explain in detail how modern air conditioners work
to signal a shift from the problem to its solutions
to give a specific example of a city with an urban heat island
items.skill: Puts sentences or events in a logical order

options: sentence 2

items.stem: Which evidence would BEST support sentence 7?
options: After planting thousands of trees, one city recorded summer street temperatures up to three degrees lower.
Many people prefer to live in the countryside because it is quieter and has much less traffic.

items.stem: Which sentence would be the BEST conclusion for the report?
options: Summer is the hottest season of the year in most countries in the northern half of the world.
Scientists use special instruments called thermometers to measure air temperatures accurately.

units.title: Narrative Time Shifts and Research from Several Sources
skills: Use transitions to show sequence and to signal shifts in time or setting
Use flashback, dialogue and precise details to develop experiences
Gather information from several sources and judge their credibility
Quote or paraphrase accurately and combine information from more than one source
vocab: flashback
a scene that interrupts the story to show an earlier event
time-shift transition
a phrase that signals a change in time: years earlier, by the next morning
setting
the time and place in which a story happens
synthesis

primary source

secondary source

passage.title: The Old Photograph
passage.intro: Saleh is writing a story. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) While cleaning the attic, I found a faded photograph of a boy standing beside a fishing boat. (2) The boy had my grandfather’s wide smile. (3) I was seven years old, sitting on his lap as he told me stories about the sea. (4) He described the storms that rocked his boat and the nights he slept under the stars. (5) I hadn’t thought about those stories in years. (6) Now, holding the photograph, I could almost hear his voice again. (7) I carried it downstairs to show my father.

items.stem: Which word in sentence 6 signals a return to the present?
options: almost
holding
Now
again
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: Which word could replace “carried” in sentence 7 to show how much the photograph meant to Saleh?
options: dropped
dragged
tossed
cradled
items.skill: Chooses precise or vivid language

items.stem: Which phrase would BEST begin sentence 3 to signal a flashback?
options: As a result of cleaning,
Suddenly, I remembered a day years earlier:
At the very same moment, up in the dusty attic,
For example, in the faded old photograph,
items.skill: Chooses a transition that connects ideas

items.stem: What is the purpose of sentences 3 and 4?
options: to show a memory that explains why the photograph matters

to describe how fishing boats are built and repaired

While cleaning the dusty attic, where sunlight slipped through one cracked window, I found a faded photograph.
items.skill: Uses narrative techniques: dialogue, description and pacing

items.stem: Which sentence could be added after sentence 7 to end the story with a meaningful reflection?
options: As my father smiled at the picture, I realized that our family’s stories live on as long as we keep telling them.

passage.title: Research Notes: The Story of Coffee
passage.intro: Ghala is writing a report using two sources. Read the sources and her draft, then answer the questions.
paras: **Source A** (a history website run by a university): “Coffee plants grew wild in Ethiopia, but people in Yemen began growing coffee on farms in the 1400s. The Yemeni port of Mocha became the center of the world coffee trade.”
**Source B** (a blog post with no author named): “Coffee was invented in France in the 1700s, and everyone in the world loved it right away.”
**Draft**

(1) Coffee has a long and interesting history. (2) The plant grew wild in Ethiopia. (3) In the 1400s, farmers in Yemen started to grow coffee as a crop. (4) Soon, the port of Mocha became the center of the coffee trade. (5) Coffeehouses then spread to cities such as Cairo and Istanbul. (6) Today, coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world.

items.stem: Which source is MORE credible?
options: Source B, because it says that everyone in the world loved coffee right away
Source A, because it was written in the present tense
Source A, because it comes from a university and gives specific facts
Source B, because it is shorter and easier to understand quickly
items.skill: Chooses a useful source or research question

items.stem: Which sentence from the draft is supported by Source A?
options: sentence 1
sentence 3
sentence 5
sentence 6
items.skill: Uses notes and facts accurately in writing

items.stem: Which sentence needs support from another credible source because neither source mentions it?
options: sentence 2
sentence 3
sentence 4
sentence 5
items.skill: Chooses a useful source or research question

items.stem: Why should Ghala NOT use Source B?
options: It makes a claim that conflicts with a more credible source.
It is written about the long history of a very popular drink.
It uses complete sentences and correct punctuation.
It mentions a country in Europe instead of Asia.
items.skill: Chooses a useful source or research question

items.stem: Ghala wants to quote Source A directly in sentence 4. Which revision does this correctly?
options: According to a university history website, the port of Mocha “became the center of the world coffee trade.”
“According to a university history website,” the port of Mocha became the center of coffee.
The port of Mocha became the center of the world coffee trade, which is a very interesting fact that I found online.
According to a website, the port of Mocha became “the center” of the world “coffee trade.”
items.skill: Paraphrases or cites a source correctly

items.stem: Which revision of sentence 1 makes a more engaging introduction?
options: Coffee is brown, and it is hot, and people drink it in cups or mugs every day.
Every morning, millions of people sip a drink whose story began in the hills of Ethiopia.

items.skill: Chooses an effective introduction

items.stem: Which sentence would BEST conclude the report by drawing the ideas together?
options: Some people like to add milk, sugar or spices such as cardamom to their coffee to change its taste and smell.
Ethiopia is a country in East Africa with mountains, rivers and many farms.
From wild plants in Ethiopia to cafés around the globe, coffee connects many cultures and centuries.
Istanbul is a large city that sits on two continents, Europe and Asia.

vocab: verbal
a verb form used as a noun, an adjective or an adverb
gerund

participle

infinitive
to + a verb, used as a noun, adjective or adverb: to win
participial phrase

dangling participle
a participial phrase with no word in the sentence for it to describe

units.title: Active and Passive Voice and Verb Mood
skills: Form and use verbs in the active and passive voice
Form and use the indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional and subjunctive moods
Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in voice and mood
Choose voice and mood for a purpose, such as emphasis or politeness
vocab: active voice
the subject performs the action: The team won the match.
passive voice
the subject receives the action: The match was won by the team.
indicative mood
states facts or opinions: The bus leaves at seven.
imperative mood
gives commands or requests: Close the door, please.
conditional mood
shows what would happen under a condition: If it rained, we would stay inside.
subjunctive mood
expresses wishes, demands or situations contrary to fact: I wish I were taller.

units.title: Commas, Dashes and Ellipses for Pauses, Breaks and Omissions

vocab: ellipsis
three spaced dots (…) that show a pause, a trailing thought or words left out
dash
a long mark (—) that shows a sudden break or sets off information with emphasis
interrupter
a word or phrase that breaks the flow of a sentence: however, in fact
omission
words removed from a quotation, shown with an ellipsis
nonrestrictive element
extra information that can be removed without changing the main meaning
introductory element
a word, phrase or clause that comes before the main clause
